# Experimental API reference

platoon.experimental: documented API that a minor release may still change (RFC 0017, section 2).

For now, task samplers and the per-task statistics they read (RFC 0019, section 5): a sampler class
(`Sampler`, or any class of the `TaskSampler` protocol) answers each decision with a task of its pool
(`Draw`) or, from a run's sampler that hands its slots to the entries, a `Slot`; it is registered with
`task_sampler` from a module an environment entry's `package` names, or named as `module:Class`, and
`platoon.testing.check_task_sampler` checks it against the contract.  An adaptive sampler reads the statistics
through a `TaskStatsView`; `TaskStatsStore` and the record types let a test build one.
`docs/extending/task-samplers.md` is the guide.

And group admission rules (RFC 0019, section 6): a rule class (`AdmissionRule`, or any class of the
`GroupAdmission` protocol) decides, for each settled training group and the statistics' view, whether it counts
toward the batch (`Admission`, or a bool); it is built with an `AdmissionSetup`, may refuse a config
in its load-time `check` (`AdmissionCheckContext`), is registered with `group_admission` or named as
`module:Class`, and `platoon.testing.check_group_admission` checks it.  `docs/extending/group-admission.md` is the
guide.

And rollout leases (RFC 0020): a training workflow runs each of its rollouts on one of its draw's rollout permits, in
a block of the draw's lease (`RolloutLease`, which `rollout_lease` reads in the workflow's task), so that
under `train.permit_release: rollout` each permit comes back as its rollout ends.
`docs/extending/rollout-leases.md` is the guide.

And trainers (RFC 0021): what `platoon train` runs (`Trainer`), built from what it prepared
(`TrainerSetup`: the config, each policy's `PolicySpec` by its id, `MAIN` for `train:`'s, the
run's `TaskSources` and how its `Workflows` are built), saying what it asks of the run
(`TrainerNeeds`) and where its steps end (`StepPlan`).  `TrainerBase` takes a trainer through the
lifecycle every trainer shares, calling its hooks in order, and `platoon.testing.check_trainer` checks one.  What
every full checkpoint of the run holds besides its counters comes from its participants
(`CheckpointParticipant`), and a policy's rows train under an `Objective`.  `trainer:` selects the
trainer; this release has two, `rl` and `sft`.
And step hooks (RFC 0021): work at the end of each step of any trainer (`StepHook`, `StepHookBase`),
which hears what the step did (`StepEnd`): it drains side work, adds optimizer updates of the step's policy
(`end.train`, `end.learner`), and hears what the step published; the rl trainer attaches those its config names
(`trainer_options.hooks`).  A hook's interruptible wait raises `TrainInterrupted` on a stop request when
the trainer's steps are atomic (`TrainerNeeds.atomic_steps`); when they are not, it runs to its end.  Side inference
samples a policy's published sampler through a `PolicySnapshot`, which refuses a sample once the policy has
published again (`PolicyMoved`); and a training episode sees its draw (`ctx.draw`, a `DrawInfo`) when
its trainer asks for it.  `docs/extending/step-hooks.md` is the guide.
And the workflow contract (RFC 0021): what the trainer needs of a rollout workflow (`RolloutWorkflow`), what a
workflow class can do beyond it (`WorkflowCapabilities`, read through `capabilities_of`), what
`platoon train` builds a workflow class with (`WorkflowSetup`, which its `from_setup` takes), and how a
group's output is read: its report (`OutputReport`, `report_of`) and its rows by policy
(`RolloutOutput`, `rows_by_policy`).  A trainer that rolls out draws the run's groups through
`run.rollouts()`.
And credit estimators (RFC 0021): how an environment entry's training groups turn rewards into advantages
(`CreditEstimator`, or a subclass of `CreditEstimatorBase`), built per entry with a `CreditSetup`
and checked at load (`CreditCheckContext`); its `assign` sees a `CreditGroup` of
`MemberRollout` members, each agent an `AgentRun` (role, policy, own reward, rows), each row a
`TrainingSample`, and the run's policies as `PolicyView` views.  It is registered with
`credit_estimator` or named as `module:Class`, and `platoon.testing.check_credit_estimator` checks it.
`docs/extending/credit-estimators.md` is the guide.

This module imports neither `tinker` nor `datasets`.

```python
import platoon.experimental
```

| [`MemberResult`](#platoon-experimental-memberresult) | One member of a group: what its rollout returned. |
| [`TaskStats`](#platoon-experimental-taskstats) | One training task's statistics, read-only: what its groups add up to (the fields of `GroupTotals`), and the rest below. |
| [`TaskStatsStore`](#platoon-experimental-taskstatsstore) | The per-task statistics of a run's training tasks: what each task's groups add up to, its streaks and newest groups, its evidence decayed by policy version, and what became of each of its draws (RFC 0019, section 3.3). |
| [`informative_at`](#platoon-experimental-informative-at) | The expected chance that a group of `k` mixes passes and failures: `E[pass@k] - E[p^k]`, never below 0. |
| [`pass_at`](#platoon-experimental-pass-at) | The expected pass@k of a task whose pass rate is `Beta(alpha, beta)`: `1 - prod_{i<k} (beta + i) / (alpha + beta + i)`, for fractional, decayed counts too; pass@1 is the posterior mean. |
| [`Admission`](#platoon-experimental-admission) | A rule's decision on one settled group: `admit` it to the step that dequeues it, or reject it, with `reason`, a non-empty string of at most 64 characters, which goes into a rejection's fate event and the step's metrics. Left out, the reason is `"admitted"` or `"rejected"`, by `admit`. |
| [`AdmissionCheckContext`](#platoon-experimental-admissioncheckcontext) | What a rule's load-time `check` sees: the parts of the config a rule's rules need, as plain data. |

A rule must be a pure function of `(group, stats, options)`: it keeps no state between calls, so that a resume decides as the run would have (`platoon.testing.check_group_admission` checks it). |
| [`AdmissionSetup`](#platoon-experimental-admissionsetup) | What a rule is built with, once per start of the process: `Class(setup, options)`. |
| [`GroupAdmission`](#platoon-experimental-groupadmission) | What the trainer calls of a rule: `admit(group, stats)`, one synchronous call per settled group. |
| [`group_admission`](#platoon-experimental-group-admission) | Register a group admission rule class under `name`, from a module that an environment entry's `package` names, so that configs can name it (`group_admission: <name>`); `options` sets its `options_schema` and `check` its load-time check. Core's names (`all`, `informative`) are reserved whatever was imported first, and so is any name that reads as one of them whatever its case and its `-` or `_` (`Informative`, which a config that misspells core's name would otherwise pick up); a name registered twice is an error. |
| [`RolloutLease`](#platoon-experimental-rolloutlease) | The rollout permits of the training draw whose workflow runs in this asyncio context (`rollout_lease`). |
| [`rollout_lease`](#platoon-experimental-rollout-lease) | The lease of the training draw whose workflow runs in this asyncio context (`RolloutLease`). |
| [`Trainer`](#platoon-experimental-trainer) | What `platoon train` runs: a trainer is resolved from the config's `trainer:` (`platoon.train.trainer.registry`), built from its setup, entered with `async with`, and run once per start. Supervising the run, its restarts, the reaping of what a dead start left, the run's lock, its config snapshot and its identity check stay `platoon train`'s. |
| [`TrainerBase`](#platoon-experimental-trainerbase) | An optional base of trainers. `run()` takes the trainer through the lifecycle every trainer shares (`platoon.train.trainer.run.TrainerRun`), which calls the hooks below in order, each with the run; every hook has a default but `prepare` and `run_steps`, which a subclass writes. `async with` opens what every start logs to, the stats logger (`stats_logger`, which resumes the W&B run of the checkpoint the start resumes from) and the train tracker (`train_tracker`), and labels every sandbox the run starts with the run, so that the run's sandboxes can be reaped by it. The policies' training clients open before `prepare`, each trainable one with its optimizer's parameters. |
| [`TrainerNeeds`](#platoon-experimental-trainerneeds) | What a trainer asks of the run, which `platoon train` reads before it lists any task (RFC 0021, rule 10 for the second and third). |
| [`TrainerSetup`](#platoon-experimental-trainersetup) | What `platoon train` prepared for the trainer it builds (`Trainer.from_setup`). Building the setup does no I/O. |
| [`TaskSources`](#platoon-experimental-tasksources) | The run's tasks as `platoon train` lists them: the training tasks (`train_dataset`, a weighted order's first epoch or the listing a dataloader shuffles), the order they are drawn in epoch by epoch and the task samplers that draw them (None: the dataset as it is), and the evaluation's (None when the run evaluates nothing). |
| [`Workflows`](#platoon-experimental-workflows) | A start's rollout workflows: training's, and the evaluation's (None when the start evaluates nothing). |
| [`StepPlan`](#platoon-experimental-stepplan) | Where a start's steps end: `end_step`, the step after the run's last one (the start trains up to it); and `steps_per_epoch`, the steps of one pass over what the trainer trains on, by which `checkpoint.strategy: epoch` counts (None: a pass is a step). |
| [`PolicySpec`](#platoon-experimental-policyspec) | One policy, as the config declares it: the model, how its prompts are rendered and sampled, its Tinker service, how a new run trains it (its adapter's rank, the weights it starts from), and how each step updates it (its optimizer, and the loss its rows train under). |
| [`MAIN`](#platoon-experimental-main) | The policy that `train:` declares. The same object as `task_stats.MAIN`, by whose versions the per-task statistics age their evidence, so that their snapshots keep their format. |
| [`CheckpointParticipant`](#platoon-experimental-checkpointparticipant) | Part of the run's state that every full checkpoint saves, and that a start which resumes from one takes up. |
| [`Objective`](#platoon-experimental-objective) | What a policy's rows train under: one of the Tinker service's built-in losses (`loss_fn`, such as `cispo`) with its keyword arguments, the loss inputs the datums carry for the trainer only, and the training metrics of each microbatch. |
| [`StepHook`](#platoon-experimental-stephook) | Work at the end of each step of any trainer, after the step's own updates and its commit, before it publishes. A class of this protocol defines all four methods; subclass `StepHookBase`, whose methods are empty, to leave some out. `critical` is optional (True when left out). A hook with state to resume is also a `CheckpointParticipant`. Register it in the trainer's `check()` or `prepare()`. |
| [`StepHookBase`](#platoon-experimental-stephookbase) | An optional base of step hooks: every method empty, critical, and `from_run`, which builds a hook that the config names. |
| [`StepEnd`](#platoon-experimental-stepend) | What the end of a step tells its hooks. `hook_updates` is platoon's own count of the hooks' updates: the optimizer steps each policy took since the step's end began, whatever a hook counts. `train`, `learner` and `wait` are the run's; a test builds a step's end with `for_test`. |
| [`TrainInterrupted`](#platoon-experimental-traininterrupted) | A shutdown signal stopped the train loop where the last completed step is a consistent checkpoint. |
| [`PolicySnapshot`](#platoon-experimental-policysnapshot) | A policy's published sampler at `version`, with what renders and parses its calls. On a fully fine-tuned service a sampling client samples the newest weights whatever its path, so `sample` checks the version around each call; a trainer that samples during a step stops that work in its hook's `drain()`, before the step publishes. The check reads the version, not the weights: there, the step's own optimizer steps change what the sampler samples before the step publishes, so a sample is its version's only up to the step's first update. |
| [`PolicyMoved`](#platoon-experimental-policymoved) | A snapshot refused a sample: its policy published a newer sampler before the call, or while it ran, so the sample would not be its version's. |
| [`DrawInfo`](#platoon-experimental-drawinfo) | The run and the training draw an episode belongs to (`ctx.draw`), when its trainer asks for them (RFC 0021's draw provenance, `TrainerNeeds.draw_provenance`); never in an evaluation. A draw's key `(start, seq)` is never reused in its run, not even by a draw a resume makes again, and a step's end names the draws it committed by it (`StepEnd.consumed`). |
| [`RolloutWorkflow`](#platoon-experimental-rolloutworkflow) | What the trainer needs of a rollout workflow: one draw's task row in, its group's output out (None: the group failed, and trains nothing). The output is a `RolloutOutput`, or a sequence of datums, all of the run's one trained policy (a `GroupOutput`, or a plain list). |
| [`WorkflowCapabilities`](#platoon-experimental-workflowcapabilities) | What a workflow class can do beyond `arun_episode`, which the trainer reads (`capabilities_of`) instead of testing whether the class is a `GroupRolloutWorkflow`. A class declares them in a `capabilities` class attribute, or as class flags of the same names; `GroupRolloutWorkflow` sets seven of them as flags. |
| [`capabilities_of`](#platoon-experimental-capabilities-of) | What `workflow` (an instance or a class) can do: its `capabilities` when it declares them, else its class flags, a flag it does not set False. Each flag is read as the trainer read it before the contract was written down: `applies_entry_settings` and `runs_rollouts_on_lease` by their truth, the others only when they are True. |
| [`WorkflowSetup`](#platoon-experimental-workflowsetup) | What `platoon train` builds one phase's workflow with (a workflow class's `from_setup`), in place of `GroupRolloutWorkflow`'s keyword arguments, whose `model_info` cannot carry several policies: the phase's settings and the run's components, and the policies its rollouts sample. |
| [`RolloutOutput`](#platoon-experimental-rolloutoutput) | A group's output written to the contract: its rows, by the policy each trains, and its report. The other output a workflow may return is a sequence of datums (`GroupOutput`, a plain list). |
| [`OutputReport`](#platoon-experimental-outputreport) | What the trainer reads of a group's output besides its rows, in one place: the per-task statistics and the group admission rules read its members and verdict, the step that consumes the group its statistics and its workload, and the label metrics its label. What an output does not give is None (`members` empty, `verdict` unknown). `workload` and its four counts come together: all set, or all None. |
| [`report_of`](#platoon-experimental-report-of) | The report of a group's output: its `report` when it gives one (a `RolloutOutput`, a `GroupOutput`), else the one its attributes give (`carried_report`: an output written before the contract was, such as a workflow's own list subclass), which for a plain list of datums, or None for a group that failed, is empty. |
| [`rows_by_policy`](#platoon-experimental-rows-by-policy) | A group's rows by the policy each trains. A list of datums (a `GroupOutput`, or a workflow's plain list), or any other output without `rows()` (a tuple of datums, say), is all `trained`'s, the run's one trained policy: `{trained: output}`, the output itself. Any other output answers `rows()`. The step reads every output's rows through this one function. |
| [`CreditEstimator`](#platoon-experimental-creditestimator) | What the trainer calls of a credit estimator: `assign(group)`, once per training group, awaited. |
| [`CreditEstimatorBase`](#platoon-experimental-creditestimatorbase) | An optional base class of credit estimators: the protocol's shape, typed options and a load-time check. |
| [`CreditSetup`](#platoon-experimental-creditsetup) | What an estimator is built with, once per start of the process and environment entry: `Class(setup, options)`. |
| [`CreditCheckContext`](#platoon-experimental-creditcheckcontext) | What an estimator's load-time `check` sees, beside its options. |
| [`CreditGroup`](#platoon-experimental-creditgroup) | One training group, as its estimator sees it: its task, its label (its value of the run's label column) and its environment entry, the entry's training settings (`settings`), the members that returned a result, in the group's order, the run's policies, each policy's version when `assign` began (`versions`; it does not move during the call, although the policies may publish meanwhile), and where the group's own statistics go (`stats`: in a training group the `DeferredStats` that the step that consumes the group records, outside one the stats tracker; an estimator's metrics belong under `credit/`). |
| [`MemberRollout`](#platoon-experimental-memberrollout) | One member of the group that returned a result: its place among them (`index`), every row of its rollout (`samples`), its agents (filled when the estimator asked for them, else empty), its root's processed reward and whether that is a completed root's scored outcome (`task_reward_valid`: an interrupted root's is not, and enters no baseline), and what the converter returned (`result`), to read: its trajectories' statistics and its root's reward components. Its `datums` are the member's rows; an estimator sets their advantages through `samples`. |
| [`AgentRun`](#platoon-experimental-agentrun) | One agent of one member's rollout: its trajectory, its parent's trajectory (None for the root), its role (`policy` for the root unless its program says otherwise; a child's is the role it was minted with), the policy it samples, its depth in the tree, its reward and its rows. `reward` is its trajectory's processed reward, as the converter loaded it onto its action tokens; None when it was not scored: the agent was interrupted, or it is a child whose verifier gave no verdict (a judge error, an unparseable or a pending verdict), whose 0 is no score. An estimator never trains an unscored agent's reward as 0, nor counts it in a baseline. An agent whose rows the converter left out has no `samples`: an unscored one, and a scored child that was sampled out or that its parent did not use, whose reward still counts. |
| [`TrainingSample`](#platoon-experimental-trainingsample) | One row to train (`datum`), with who produced it: the policy that sampled it and trains on it, the member of the group whose rollout it is (its place among the members that returned a result), and, when the estimator asked for agents (`needs_agents`), the agent, its role, its trajectory and its depth in the agent tree. It lives in the trainer process only: what reaches the training service is the datum. |
| [`PolicyView`](#platoon-experimental-policyview) | What an estimator may read of a policy: its id, and the renderer that turns its token ids into text. |
| [`credit_estimator`](#platoon-experimental-credit-estimator) | Register a credit estimator class under `name`, from a module that an environment entry's `package` names, so that configs can name it (`credit: <name>`); `options` sets its `options_schema` and `check` its load-time check. Core's names (`group`, `keyed`, and `reverse_kl` and `gae`, which platoon adds) are reserved, whatever their case and their `-` or `_`; a name registered twice is an error. |

## Task samplers

The task sampler API: the classes a sampler is made of and answers with, and what it sees.

<a id="platoon-experimental-draw"></a>

### `platoon.experimental.Draw`

```python
class Draw
```

A sampler's answer: one task of its pool.  `reason` (a non-empty string of at most 64 characters) and
`score` (None or a finite number) go into the group's record (`GroupRecord.reason`, `.score`), its draw
event and the step's metrics.  A pool whose listing repeats a task id draws the first row with that id.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `task_id` | `str` | required | The task drawn: one of the decision's `ctx.task_ids`. |
| `reason` | `str` | `"order"` | Why it was drawn, as the group's record, its draw event and the step's draws by reason (draws/<reason>) keep it. |
| `score` | `float \| None` | `None` | What the sampler made of the task, None for nothing: the group's record keeps it, and pass_rate's is the chance it predicted that the group trains (predicted_informative). |

<a id="platoon-experimental-sampler"></a>

### `platoon.experimental.Sampler`

```python
class Sampler
```

An optional base class of task samplers: the protocol's defaults, and the optional hooks.  Built once per start
of the process as `Class(setup, options)`, it keeps the `SamplerSetup` as `self.setup` and the options,
parsed against `options_schema` (None without one), as `self.options`.

| Attribute | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `adaptive` | `ClassVar[bool]` | Whether it reads the run's statistics, and so decides when a group can start; False: a function of its decision index, asked when the dispatcher draws a new position. |
| `entry_slots` | `ClassVar[bool]` | Whether next() may return Slot(entry): a static run sampler only. |
| `options_schema` | `ClassVar[Any]` | Its options' schema: a dataclass, a pydantic model, or a function of the options' mapping that returns them parsed and raises ValueError; None: it takes no options. `self.options` holds them parsed. |

#### `Sampler.next`

```python
def next(ctx: SamplerContext) -> Draw | Slot | str | None
```

Answer one decision: a `Draw` of a task of `ctx.task_ids` (for an adaptive sampler, one that
`ctx.eligible` accepts), or that task's id; from a static run sampler whose class sets `entry_slots`,
a `Slot` that hands the draw to an entry's sampler; None only when nothing is eligible.  One synchronous
call, its randomness taken from `ctx.rng` or `ctx.key`; an answer outside these, or an exception, gets the
dispatcher's fallback draw.

#### `Sampler.observe`

```python
def observe(group: GroupRecord) -> None
```

A settled group of its pool, in draw order (adaptive samplers only), before its next decision and before
every save; it must also work without them.

#### `Sampler.state_dict`

```python
def state_dict() -> dict[str, Any]
```

What it keeps between decisions, as JSON data: nothing.

#### `Sampler.load_state_dict`

```python
def load_state_dict(state: Mapping[str, Any]) -> None
```

Take up what `state_dict` saved: nothing; a `ValueError` for any other state.

#### `Sampler.metrics`

```python
def metrics(stats: TaskStatsView | None) -> Mapping[str, float]
```

Its metrics of the step, each a finite number, which every step logs under its prefix
(`train/sampler/<key>` for the run's sampler, `train/sampler/environment/<entry>/<key>` for an entry's):
called once a step with the statistics' view for an adaptive sampler, with None for a static one.  The keys
the dispatcher writes itself there (`RESERVED_METRICS`, and `draws/...`) are left out, with an error
logged once.  None by default.

#### `Sampler.check`

```python
@staticmethod
def check(options: Any, ctx: SamplerCheckContext) -> None
```

Refuse a config it cannot serve, with a `ValueError` that says why: it accepts every config.

<a id="platoon-experimental-samplercheckcontext"></a>

### `platoon.experimental.SamplerCheckContext`

```python
class SamplerCheckContext
```

What a sampler's load-time `check` sees: the parts of the config a sampler's rules need, as plain data.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `level` | `Level` | required | The level it is checked at: the run's sampler ("run") or an entry's ("entry"). |
| `entry` | `str \| None` | required | The entry, at the entry level. |
| `run_sampler` | `str` | required | train.task_sampler as written ("auto" when unset). |
| `entries` | `Mapping[str, Mapping[str, Any]]` | required | Every entry by label, in config order, each exactly {"weight": a number or "tasks", "seed": int, "group_size": int (the entry's training group size), "success_threshold": float, "task_sampler": str \| None, "task_sampler_options": dict}. A check runs before the tasks are listed, so a weight is as written. |
| `batch_size` | `int` | required | The run's train.batch_size. |
| `label_column` | `str` | required | The column the run's labels come from (train.label_by). |

<a id="platoon-experimental-samplercontext"></a>

### `platoon.experimental.SamplerContext`

```python
class SamplerContext
```

What one decision sees.  A decision is one synchronous call; it must not keep the context.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `task_ids` | `Sequence[str]` | required | The candidates: the sampler's whole pool (SamplerSetup.task_ids), in listing order. Eligibility is the predicate below, never a filtered list, so that an index means the same in every decision. |
| `entry` | `str \| None` | required | The entry whose tasks it chooses among, at the entry level; None at the run level. |
| `decision` | `int` | required | This sampler's decision index, 0-based, saved and restored: it advances whenever a draw or a slot binds for it, its own or the fallback's, and never for a None while nothing is eligible. |
| `key` | `int` | required | decision_key(seed, name, decision): what the decision's randomness follows from (a sampler that brings numpy seeds numpy.random.Generator(numpy.random.Philox(key)) with it). |
| `eligible` | `Callable[[str], bool]` | required | Whether a task may be chosen now: its label is below its limit; always true for a static sampler, whose draws may wait for their label. |
| `stats` | `TaskStatsView \| None` | required | The run's per-task statistics, which only an adaptive sampler reads (TaskStatsView); None for a static one. |
| `step` | `int` | required | The training steps committed. |
| `versions` | `Mapping[str, int]` | required | The policy version now, by policy: {"main": version}. |

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `str` | required | Its qualified name: the run's sampler as the config names it ("auto", "weighted", "pass_rate", "acme.s:Mine"), an entry's with the entry's label ("uniform@quick", "pass_rate@hard"). |

| `batch_size` | `int` | required | The run's train.batch_size. |
| `label_column` | `str` | required | The column the run's labels come from (train.label_by), whose label limits eligibility follows. |
| `seed` | `int` | required | The seed its decisions' keys follow from (SamplerContext.key): the entry's seed at the entry level, 0 at the run level, plus its parsed options' seed when they have an integer one (as pass_rate's do), so a sampler with a seed option reads it here and need not add it again. |

<a id="platoon-experimental-taskstatsview"></a>

### `platoon.experimental.TaskStatsView`

```python
class TaskStatsView
```

The run's per-task statistics as an adaptive sampler reads them, at policy version `now`: read-only, every
result a value of its own.  `live` is False when the statistics stopped in this start (the view reads what they
held) or never started (it reads an empty store over the pool).

`counts` is the cheap read (a task's counts and streaks, read from its record); `task` builds the
task's whole record, so a decision that reads it for every task of a large pool spends time in proportion to the
pool: read `counts` for every task, and `task` for a few.

| Attribute | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `now` | `int` | The policy version the view reads at. Read-only. |
| `live` | `bool` | False when the statistics stopped in this start, or never started: then the view reads what they held, or nothing. Read-only. |

#### `TaskStatsView.task_ids`

```python
def task_ids() -> tuple[str, ...]
```

Every training task of the run, in pool order.

#### `TaskStatsView.counts`

```python
def counts(task_id: str) -> TaskCounts
```

The task's counts and streaks (`platoon.train.task_stats.TaskCounts`), read without building
anything: the read to make for every task of a pool.  `KeyError` for a task the statistics do not hold.

#### `TaskStatsView.task`

```python
def task(task_id: str) -> TaskStats
```

The task's whole record (`platoon.train.task_stats.TaskStats`): attempts, passes, kinds, fates, the
newest groups and decayed means, built afresh, so read it for a few tasks only.  `KeyError` for a task the
statistics do not hold.

#### `TaskStatsView.posterior`

```python
def posterior(task_id: str) -> tuple[float, float]
```

`(alpha, beta)` of the task's posterior pass rate at `now`: its decayed passes and failures over a
prior of weight 2 at its entry's decayed pass rate.

#### `TaskStatsView.entry`

```python
def entry(name: str) -> GroupTotals
```

What the groups of entry `name` add up to.

#### `TaskStatsView.label`

```python
def label(label: str) -> GroupTotals
```

What the groups of the tasks labelled `label` add up to.

#### `TaskStatsView.labels`

```python
def labels() -> tuple[str, ...]
```

The labels of the run's training tasks.

#### `TaskStatsView.group_size`

```python
def group_size(entry: str | None) -> int
```

Entry `entry`'s training group size (None: the run's).

#### `TaskStatsView.threshold`

```python
def threshold(entry: str | None) -> float
```

The reward at or above which a rollout of entry `entry` passes (its `success_threshold`).

<a id="platoon-experimental-task-sampler"></a>

### `platoon.experimental.task_sampler`

```python
def task_sampler(
    name: str,
    *,
    options: Any = None,
    check: Callable[[Any, SamplerCheckContext], None] | None = None,
) -> Callable[[S], S]
```

Register a sampler class under `name`, from a module that an environment entry's `package` names, so that
configs can name it (`task_sampler: <name>`); `options` sets its `options_schema` and `check` its load-time
check.  Core's names (`auto`, `weighted`, `uniform`, `pass_rate`) are reserved whatever was imported first,
and so is any name that reads as one of them whatever its case and its `-` or `_` (`Pass-Rate`, which a
config that misspells core's name would otherwise pick up); a name registered twice is an error.

The records and the store an adaptive sampler reads through its view.

<a id="platoon-experimental-grouprecord"></a>

### `platoon.experimental.GroupRecord`

```python
class GroupRecord
```

One settled group: which draw it was, and what its members did.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `start` | `int` | required | Which start of the run drew it: (start, seq) is unique in a run. |
| `seq` | `int` | required | Its draw's number within that start. |
| `task_id` | `str` | required | The task it ran. |
| `entry` | `str \| None` | required | The environment entry it ran (its label). |
| `labels` | `Mapping[str, str]` | required | Its labels: {label column: label}. |
| `harness` | `str \| None` | required | The harness it ran, when known. |
| `group_size` | `int` | required | How many rollouts the group ran. |
| `sampler` | `str` | required | The task sampler that drew it: the run's sampler as the config names it (train.task_sampler, "auto" by default), or an entry's, "<sampler>@<entry>" ("uniform@quick", "pass_rate@hard"). |
| `reason` | `str` | required | Why it was drawn: "order" for a static order's draw, "explore" or "exploit" for pass_rate's, "fallback" for one the dispatcher drew after the sampler's decision failed, "reissue" for a draw a resume drew again, or a custom sampler's own. |
| `score` | `float \| None` | required | The sampler's score of the draw, None without one (pass_rate's: the chance it predicted that the group trains). |
| `position` | `int \| None` | required | The draw's place in the run's order; a reissued draw keeps its old one. |
| `drawn_at` | `Mapping[str, int]` | required | The policy versions when it was drawn, by policy. |
| `members` | `tuple[MemberResult, ...]` | required | What each of its rollouts did. |
| `verdict` | `str` | required | The workflow's verdict (VERDICTS). |
| `valid` | `int` | | Its valid members. Read-only. |

Its valid members whose scored reward reaches `threshold`.

The oldest policy version its datums sampled (the stale filter's reference), else the one it was drawn at.

#### `GroupRecord.kind`

```python

```

What the group was, by the step metrics' partition of the groups that trained or were uniform:
`informative`, `all_pass`, `all_fail` or `uniform_mixed`; None for another verdict.

The record as JSON data, as a checkpoint's kept groups keep it (`from_json` reads it back).

The record `to_json` wrote.

<a id="platoon-experimental-memberresult"></a>

### `platoon.experimental.MemberResult`

```python
class MemberResult
```

One member of a group: what its rollout returned.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `reward` | `float \| None` | required | The root's reward as trained, after the reward processor; None: no result (a setup failure, a dead worker, a cancelled straggler). |
| `scored` | `float \| None` | required | The reward its environment scored, before any reward processor, as platoon eval judges success; None when its outcome was not scored. |
| `valid` | `bool` | required | Whether its root completed with a scored outcome, so that it entered the baseline. |
| `outcome` | `str` | required | The status of its root's outcome: scored, invalid, error, timeout, cancelled, or none without one. |
| `disposition` | `str` | required | How it ended: completed, straggler_killed, worker_crashed, and the rest of the worker dispositions. |
| `reward_key` | `str \| None` | required | The reward key its root trained, if any. |
| `steps` | `int \| None` | required | Its root's steps, when known. |
| `output_tokens` | `int \| None` | required | Its root's output tokens, when known. |
| `seconds` | `float \| None` | required | Its rollout's seconds, when known. |
| `versions` | `Mapping[str, tuple[int, int]]` | `{}` | The oldest and newest policy version its datums sampled, by policy. |
| `flag` | `bool` | `False` | Whether `scored` is the rollout's own success flag, of a rollout whose trace records no outcome: platoon eval counts such a flag as a pass at 1, whatever the threshold, and so does `passes`. |

#### `MemberResult.passes`


Whether it passed: valid, with a scored reward that reaches `threshold` (1 for a rollout's own success
flag, `flag`), as platoon eval judges success.

<a id="platoon-experimental-taskstatsstore"></a>

### `platoon.experimental.TaskStatsStore`

```python
class TaskStatsStore
```

The per-task statistics of a run's training tasks: what each task's groups add up to, its streaks and newest
groups, its evidence decayed by policy version, and what became of each of its draws (RFC 0019, section 3.3).

`tasks` are the run's training tasks, in pool order: `(task id, entry, label)` each, the entry its environment
entry's label and the label its value of the run's label column.  `entries` say each entry's group size and
success threshold; `group_size` is the run's, for a task of no entry.  The trainer `draw`\s each group's
task, `settle`\s each group's record, and gives each draw its fate (`fate`); `snapshot` and
`load` save and restore it, which the trainer does at each full checkpoint.

| Attribute | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `outstanding` | `list[tuple[int, int, str, int \| None]]` | The draws no committed step has consumed: `(start, seq, task id, position)` each, in draw order. Read-only. |

#### `TaskStatsStore.draw`

```python
def draw(start: int, seq: int, task_id: str, position: int | None = None) -> None
```

A group of `task_id` was drawn, as draw `seq` of start `start`.

#### `TaskStatsStore.settle`

```python
def settle(record: GroupRecord) -> None
```

Count a settled group: its task's record, its entry's totals and its label's.

#### `TaskStatsStore.fate`

```python
def fate(start: int, seq: int, fate: str, task_id: str | None = None) -> None
```

What became of draw `seq` of start `start` (FATES).  A skipped row was never outstanding: name its
`task_id`.

#### `TaskStatsStore.reissue`

```python
def reissue(old: Sequence[int], new: tuple[int, int]) -> bool
```

A resume draws outstanding draw `old` (`(start, seq)`) again as draw `new`, of the same task at the
same position: the same draw of its task, under a new number, so it is neither counted as drawn twice nor given
a fate.  False, changing nothing, when `old` is not outstanding.

#### `TaskStatsStore.lose_outstanding`

```python
def lose_outstanding() -> list[tuple[int, int]]
```

Count every outstanding draw as lost (a resume that cannot draw them again: its checkpoint saved no
dispatcher's state); returns them, `(start, seq)` each.

#### `TaskStatsStore.threshold`

```python
def threshold(entry: str | None) -> float
```

The reward at or above which a rollout of entry `entry` passes (1.0 for a task of no entry).

#### `TaskStatsStore.group_size`

```python
def group_size(entry: str | None) -> int
```

Entry `entry`'s training group size (the run's for a task of no entry).

#### `TaskStatsStore.task_ids`

```python
def task_ids() -> list[str]
```

Every training task, in pool order.

#### `TaskStatsStore.task`

```python
def task(task_id: str) -> TaskStats
```

The task's whole record, built afresh (`counts` is the cheap read).  `KeyError` for a task the
store does not hold.

#### `TaskStatsStore.counts`

```python
def counts(task_id: str) -> TaskCounts
```

The task's counts and streaks, read from its record without building anything: the cheap read of a task,
which a task sampler makes for every task of its pool (`task` builds the whole record).

#### `TaskStatsStore.entry`

```python
def entry(name: str) -> GroupTotals
```

What the groups of entry `name` add up to.

#### `TaskStatsStore.label`

```python
def label(label: str) -> GroupTotals
```

What the groups of the tasks labelled `label` add up to.

#### `TaskStatsStore.labels`

```python
def labels() -> list[str]
```

The labels of the training tasks.

#### `TaskStatsStore.posterior`

```python
def posterior(task_id: str, *, now: int) -> tuple[float, float]
```

`(alpha, beta)` of the task's posterior pass rate at policy version `now`: its decayed passes and
failures over a prior centered on its entry's decayed pass rate (the run's, for a task of no entry).

#### `TaskStatsStore.step_metrics`

```python
def step_metrics(*, now: int, prefixes: Mapping[str, str]) -> dict[str, float]
```

The `tasks/` metrics of a step at policy version `now`: over every task (`tasks/...`) and over each
label's (`tasks/<prefix>/...`, `prefixes` mapping each logged label to its metric prefix): the mean expected
pass@1 and pass@G (G each task's entry's group size) over the seen tasks, those with a group whose members were
recorded (a custom workflow's plain list of datums records none), the share of tasks seen (`coverage`), the
seen tasks by posterior pass rate (`bands/<band>`, BANDS), and the tasks without evidence
(`no_evidence`).

#### `TaskStatsStore.snapshot`

```python
def snapshot(*, start: int, next_seq: int) -> dict[str, Any]
```

The store as JSON data, with the start that writes it and its next draw's number.

#### `TaskStatsStore.from_snapshot`

```python
@classmethod
def from_snapshot(data: Mapping[str, Any]) -> TaskStatsStore
```

The store a `snapshot` holds, its pool the tasks it holds (`platoon tasks`); a `ValueError` for
data it cannot read.

#### `TaskStatsStore.load`

```python
def load(data: Mapping[str, Any]) -> None
```

Restore what a `snapshot` holds: the records of the tasks still in the pool, every total and the
outstanding draws.  A task the snapshot does not hold starts empty; one that left the pool is dropped.  A
`ValueError` for data it cannot read.

<a id="platoon-experimental-informative-at"></a>

### `platoon.experimental.informative_at`

```python
def informative_at(alpha: float, beta: float, k: int) -> float
```

The expected chance that a group of `k` mixes passes and failures: `E[pass@k] - E[p^k]`, never below 0.

<a id="platoon-experimental-pass-at"></a>

### `platoon.experimental.pass_at`

```python
def pass_at(alpha: float, beta: float, k: int) -> float
```

The expected pass@k of a task whose pass rate is `Beta(alpha, beta)`: `1 - prod_{i<k} (beta + i) / (alpha + beta + i)`, for fractional, decayed counts too; pass@1 is the posterior mean.

## Group admission

The group admission API: a rule's answer, its base class and protocol, what it is built with, what its check sees, and the decorator that registers it.

<a id="platoon-experimental-admission"></a>

### `platoon.experimental.Admission`

```python
class Admission
```

A rule's decision on one settled group: `admit` it to the step that dequeues it, or reject it, with
`reason`, a non-empty string of at most 64 characters, which goes into a rejection's fate event and the step's
metrics.  Left out, the reason is `"admitted"` or `"rejected"`, by `admit`.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `admit` | `bool` | required |  |
| `reason` | `str \| None` | `None` |  |

<a id="platoon-experimental-admissioncheckcontext"></a>

### `platoon.experimental.AdmissionCheckContext`

```python
class AdmissionCheckContext
```

What a rule's load-time `check` sees: the parts of the config a rule's rules need, as plain data.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `level` | `Level` | required | "run" for the run's rule (train.group_admission), "entry" for an entry's own. |
| `entry` | `str \| None` | required | The entry, at the entry level. |
| `entries` | `Mapping[str, Mapping[str, Any]]` | required | Every entry by label, in config order, each exactly {"weight", "seed", "group_size", "success_threshold", "task_sampler", "task_sampler_options"}, as a task sampler's check sees them. |
| `batch_size` | `int` | required | train.batch_size: the admitted groups a step trains. |
| `label_column` | `str` | required | The column of the training tasks whose value labels a group (train.label_by; the entry by default). |
| `max_groups_per_step` | `float` | required | train.refill.max_groups_per_step. |
| `workflow_gives_verdicts` | `bool` | required | Whether the run's workflow gives each group a verdict (a GroupRolloutWorkflow, or a class that declares gives_verdicts = True). |

<a id="platoon-experimental-admissionrule"></a>

### `platoon.experimental.AdmissionRule`

```python
class AdmissionRule
```

An optional base class of group admission rules: the protocol's shape, typed options and a load-time check.  A
rule must be a pure function of `(group, stats, options)`: it keeps no state between calls, so that a resume
decides as the run would have (`platoon.testing.check_group_admission` checks it).

| Attribute | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `options_schema` | `ClassVar[Any]` | Its options' schema: a dataclass, a pydantic model, or a function of the options' mapping that returns them parsed and raises ValueError; None: it takes no options. `self.options` holds them parsed. |

#### `AdmissionRule.admit`

```python
def admit(group: GroupRecord, stats: TaskStatsView) -> Admission | bool
```

Whether `group` counts toward the batch, read against `stats` (`GroupAdmission.admit`): a subclass
implements it.

#### `AdmissionRule.check`

```python
@staticmethod
def check(options: Any, ctx: AdmissionCheckContext) -> None
```

Refuse a config it cannot serve, with a `ValueError` that says why: it accepts every config.

<a id="platoon-experimental-admissionsetup"></a>

### `platoon.experimental.AdmissionSetup`

```python
class AdmissionSetup
```

What a rule is built with, once per start of the process: `Class(setup, options)`.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `str` | required | Its qualified name: the run's rule as the config names it ("informative", "acme.rules:Quota"), an entry's with the entry's label ("informative@hard"). |
| `level` | `Level` | required | "run" for the run's rule (train.group_admission), which decides the groups of every entry that sets none; "entry" for an entry's own. |
| `entry` | `str \| None` | required | The entry, at the entry level. |
| `entries` | `Mapping[str, EntryInfo]` | required | The run's entries with training tasks, by label in config order (what the run's task samplers know of them, their task ids included); empty for a trainer given an order without sampling, so a rule must not rely on it. |
| `batch_size` | `int` | required | train.batch_size: the admitted groups a step trains. |
| `label_column` | `str` | required | The column of the training tasks whose value labels a group (train.label_by; the entry by default), the key of a group's labels (GroupRecord.labels, empty for a single environment's groups). |

<a id="platoon-experimental-groupadmission"></a>

### `platoon.experimental.GroupAdmission`

```python
class GroupAdmission(Protocol)
```

What the trainer calls of a rule: `admit(group, stats)`, one synchronous call per settled group.

#### `GroupAdmission.admit`

```python
def admit(group: GroupRecord, stats: TaskStatsView) -> Admission | bool
```

Whether `group`, a settled training group, counts toward the batch, read against `stats`, the run's
per-task statistics as of their last flush: an `Admission`, or `True` (admitted) or `False`
(rejected, reason `rejected`).  A pure function of the group, the view and the rule's options.

<a id="platoon-experimental-group-admission"></a>

### `platoon.experimental.group_admission`

```python
def group_admission(
    name: str,
    *,
    options: Any = None,
    check: Callable[[Any, AdmissionCheckContext], None] | None = None,
) -> Callable[[R], R]
```

Register a group admission rule class under `name`, from a module that an environment entry's `package`
names, so that configs can name it (`group_admission: <name>`); `options` sets its `options_schema` and
`check` its load-time check.  Core's names (`all`, `informative`) are reserved whatever was imported first,
and so is any name that reads as one of them whatever its case and its `-` or `_` (`Informative`, which a
config that misspells core's name would otherwise pick up); a name registered twice is an error.

## Rollout leases

The lease a training workflow runs each of its rollouts on, and how it reads it ([Run rollouts on the lease](../extending/rollout-leases.md)).

<a id="platoon-experimental-rolloutlease"></a>

### `platoon.experimental.RolloutLease`

```python
class RolloutLease(Protocol)
```

The rollout permits of the training draw whose workflow runs in this asyncio context (`rollout_lease`).

A draw reserves `size` rollout permits of the run's `train.max_concurrent_rollouts`: its entry's group size.
`async with lease.rollout(i):` runs rollout `i` on one of them: the block waits until the draw holds a permit
that no other block uses (at once when the run grants the draw's permits together), runs on it, and returns it to
the run as it exits, so that another draw can start.  Its value is the seconds it waited for that permit: 0.0 when
it entered at once.  Under `train.permit_release: group` a draw's blocks hold nothing and its permits come back
together when its workflow returns; outside a training draw the lease has size 0 and its blocks hold nothing,
whatever their index.

The rules a workflow keeps:

1. **One block per rollout, around the whole rollout.**  The permit stands for the rollout's worker and sandboxes:
   exit the block only once they are gone, and a cancelled rollout only once its cancellation has been awaited.  A
   rollout's retry stays inside its block.
2. **Each index once, at most `size` of them.**  In a training draw, `rollout(i)` raises `IndexError` for an
   index outside `0 .. size - 1`, and a second block for an index raises `RuntimeError` as it enters.
3. **The flag.**  A workflow class whose every rollout runs in a block says so with
   `runs_rollouts_on_lease = True`, and its draws are then granted their permits one at a time as they free
   (rolling starts); any other draw is granted whole before `arun_episode` starts, and each of its blocks still
   returns its permit.
4. **The rest comes back with the draw.**  Whatever the draw still holds comes back when `arun_episode`
   returns, raises or is cancelled; a block that enters after that, or still waits for its permit then, holds
   nothing, and the trainer warns.
5. **Read it in the task.**  The lease lives in a context variable, which asyncio tasks copy when they are
   created and `loop.run_in_executor` does not: read `rollout_lease()` in the workflow's task, before handing
   work to a thread.

Asking for permits beyond `size`, for a draw whose size varies or for an episode's child agents, is reserved for
a later release (RFC 0020).

| Attribute | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `size` | `int` | The rollout permits the draw reserved: its entry's group size; 0 outside a training draw. Read-only. |

#### `RolloutLease.rollout`

```python
def rollout(index: int) -> AbstractAsyncContextManager[float]
```

A block that runs rollout `index` of the draw on one of its permits (see the class docstring).

<a id="platoon-experimental-rollout-lease"></a>

### `platoon.experimental.rollout_lease`

```python
def rollout_lease() -> RolloutLease
```

The lease of the training draw whose workflow runs in this asyncio context (`RolloutLease`).

Outside a training draw (evaluation, a test, a direct call) a lease of size 0 whose blocks enter at once and hold
nothing, so a workflow runs its rollouts the same way everywhere.  Read it in the workflow's own task: a thread of
`loop.run_in_executor` does not see it unless the context is copied.

## Trainers

The trainer API: what platoon train runs, what it builds a trainer with, the base class whose lifecycle calls a trainer's hooks, the policies' specs, the parts of the run's state every full checkpoint holds, and what a policy's rows train under.

<a id="platoon-experimental-trainer"></a>

### `platoon.experimental.Trainer`

```python
class Trainer(Protocol)
```

What `platoon train` runs: a trainer is resolved from the config's `trainer:`
(`platoon.train.trainer.registry`), built from its setup, entered with `async with`, and run once per start.
Supervising the run, its restarts, the reaping of what a dead start left, the run's lock, its config snapshot and
its identity check stay `platoon train`'s.

#### `Trainer.needs`

```python
@classmethod
def needs(config: Any, options: Any) -> platoon.train.trainer.api.TrainerNeeds
```

#### `Trainer.from_setup`

```python
@classmethod
def from_setup(setup: platoon.train.trainer.api.TrainerSetup) -> Self
```

#### `Trainer.run`

```python
async def run() -> None
```

<a id="platoon-experimental-trainerbase"></a>

### `platoon.experimental.TrainerBase`

```python
class TrainerBase
```

An optional base of trainers.  `run()` takes the trainer through the lifecycle every trainer shares
(`platoon.train.trainer.run.TrainerRun`), which calls the hooks below in order, each with the run; every
hook has a default but `prepare` and `run_steps`, which a subclass writes.  `async with` opens what every
start logs to, the stats logger (`stats_logger`, which resumes the W&B run of the checkpoint the start
resumes from) and the train tracker (`train_tracker`), and labels every sandbox the run starts with the run,
so that the run's sandboxes can be reaped by it.  The policies' training clients open before `prepare`, each
trainable one with its optimizer's parameters.

| Attribute | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `setup` | `platoon.train.trainer.api.TrainerSetup \| None` | What the trainer was built with; None for a trainer built with a constructor of its own, outside platoon train. |
| `config` | `Any` |  |
| `options` | `Any` |  |
| `policies` | `PolicySet` | The run's policies, registered as the trainer is built. |
| `stats_logger` | `StatsLogger` | The run's stats logger, which `async with` opens: each step's metrics go to it (`log(step=, stats=)`). Read-only. |
| `train_tracker` | `StatsTracker` | The run's train tracker, which `async with` opens: what a step records (a learner's metrics among it), until the step exports it. Read-only. |
| `run_log_path` | `str` | The run directory, `log_path/<stats.experiment_name>/<stats.trial_name>`, where the run writes everything: its checkpoints, its rollouts and its logs. Read-only. |

#### `TrainerBase.needs`

```python
@classmethod
def needs(config: Any, options: Any) -> platoon.train.trainer.api.TrainerNeeds
```

What the trainer asks of the run: by default, nothing to roll out.

#### `TrainerBase.from_setup`

```python
@classmethod
def from_setup(setup: platoon.train.trainer.api.TrainerSetup) -> Self
```

#### `TrainerBase.run`

```python
async def run() -> None
```

Run this start of the run: the lifecycle every trainer shares, with this trainer's hooks.

#### `TrainerBase.check`

```python
def check(run: TrainerRun) -> None
```

1. Before any service opens: raise `ConfigError` for what the trainer cannot run.  Participants of the
run's checkpoints registered here (`run.checkpoints.register`) take up the start point before any training
client opens; step hooks may register here too (`run.hooks.register`), or in `prepare`.

#### `TrainerBase.prepare`

```python
async def prepare(run: TrainerRun, start: StartPoint) -> platoon.train.trainer.api.StepPlan
```

5. The policies are open at `start`: prepare the steps, and say where they end.  A trainer that rolls out
opens the start's draws here (`run.rollouts()`: the run's training groups, which take part in every full
checkpoint), and starts them as its steps begin.

#### `TrainerBase.started`

```python
async def started(run: TrainerRun) -> None
```

6. The launch save is done (`run.launch_save`), before each policy's first sampler.

#### `TrainerBase.ready`

```python
async def ready(run: TrainerRun) -> None
```

7. Just before the steps: the run's clock starts (`platoon.train.trainer.run.TrainerRun.start_clock`),
which a trainer that overrides this hook starts too.

#### `TrainerBase.run_steps`

```python
async def run_steps(run: TrainerRun) -> None
```

8. The steps, from `run.clock.step` to `run.clock.end`, stopping at a step boundary once a stop is asked
for (`run.shutdown`); a step awaits the service with `run.wait`.  Each step ends with `run.end_step`: the
step hooks, the publication of the policies it updated, and the clock's advance.  Steps that the stop request
stopped short of the end were interrupted: the run then saves `<step>_interrupted`, also when they did not set
`run.interrupted`, which an interrupt of their own sets, and so does a `TrainInterrupted` they raise.  The
run stops the clock's watchdog after them.

#### `TrainerBase.close`

```python
async def close(run: TrainerRun) -> None
```

10. After the save at exit, and after a failure too (`run.ended` says which): close what the trainer
opened.  The run's step hooks and participants close after it.

<a id="platoon-experimental-trainerneeds"></a>

### `platoon.experimental.TrainerNeeds`

```python
class TrainerNeeds
```

What a trainer asks of the run, which `platoon train` reads before it lists any task (RFC 0021, rule 10 for
the second and third).

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rollouts` | `bool` | `False` | Whether it trains on rollouts of the run's training tasks: then the run lists them, builds the training workflow, and opens the start's draws when the trainer asks for them (run.rollouts()). |
| `atomic_steps` | `bool` | `True` | Whether its steps reach a checkpoint whole or not at all: once a step sent training work, an interrupt saves no <step>_interrupted checkpoint of it, and the resume starts from the last full one. The rl trainer's are not. |
| `fail_closed_updates` | `bool` | `True` | Whether an optimizer step that the service skipped, or whose metrics are not finite, raises (UpdateRejected) before anything publishes, for every update, the step hooks' too. The rl trainer only logs such metrics. |
| `draw_provenance` | `bool` | `False` | Whether each training episode sees its draw (ctx.draw: platoon.programs.DrawInfo), the key that a step's end names it by (StepEnd.consumed). Off, the rollouts' requests are as they always were. |

### `platoon.experimental.PolicySpec`


One policy, as the config declares it: the model, how its prompts are rendered and sampled, its Tinker service,

| Field | Type | Default | Description |

| `id` | `str` | required |  |
| `model_name` | `str` | required |  |
| `renderer_name` | `str` | required |  |

| `sample_timeout_seconds` | `float \| None` | `None` |  |

| `load_optimizer_state` | `bool` | `False` | With load_checkpoint_path: whether the new run takes that checkpoint's optimizer state too (Adam's moments), a new trial that goes on from it; else its optimizer starts fresh. |
| `optimizer` | `AdamParams \| None` | `None` | Its optimizer's settings, the loss its rows train under (its objective's, platoon.train.objectives) and the loss's keyword arguments; each None: the run's train.optimizer, train.loss_fn or train.loss_fn_config, which policy_specs puts in its place, so that the trainer reads them from the spec alone. |
| `loss_fn` | `str \| None` | `None` |  |
| `loss_fn_config` | `dict[str, Any] \| None` | `None` |  |

### `platoon.experimental.StepHook`

```python
class StepHook(Protocol)
```

Work at the end of each step of any trainer, after the step's own updates and its commit, before it publishes.
A class of this protocol defines all four methods; subclass `StepHookBase`, whose methods are empty, to
leave some out.  `critical` is optional (True when left out).  A hook with state to resume is also a

| Attribute | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|


Finish or stop the side work that samples the current sampler, before the step's hooks update the policy
and it publishes.  Raising fails the start before anything publishes.

#### `StepHook.update`

```python

```

Optimizer updates of the run's policies, through `end.train(...)` or `end.learner(...)` only.  Raising
fails the start before anything publishes.

#### `StepHook.published`

```python
async def published(end: StepEnd) -> None
```

At every step's end, after it published (`end.published`, empty when nothing did); and once after the
launch's first sampler (`end.kind` `"launch"`).

#### `StepHook.aclose`

```python
async def aclose() -> None
```

At the start's end, also after a failure: close what the hook opened.
